newsitem.title: DUBAI: Young Germans in UAE train as camel-jockeys.
newsitem.headline: Young Germans in UAE train as camel-jockeys.

text.p: Thirty young Germans are training to become camel-jockeys in the desert of the United Arab Emirates, getting in shape for Europe's first camel race due to be held this summer.

Hans-Joachim Fuchtel, a parliamentarian from Germany's Black Forest region, said the race would take place in Berlin, Munich or the southern spa town of Baden-Baden. He said the camels would come from Europe's only camel farm in the small southern town of Rotfelden, part of his home constituency.
The camel-jockeys were mostly women and all aged between 17 and 25, Fuchtel told Reuters during a visit to the UAE.

"We recruited them from sports colleges and riding schools and they have been training here for three weeks," he said. "The exact date for the European race hasn't been set yet. It all depends on how the camels are feeling."

Fuchtel said the camel farm, now home to some 80 camels, was set up 10 years ago, and included camels from far-flung countries including Kazakhstan and the UAE, where camel races are a national pastime.

"UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan heard about it and donated 19 racing camels last year. They had to hire a special large-cabin cargo plane to transport the animals to Europe," he said.
"They were in quarantine for four months and arrived at the farm in November," he said. "Many are now pregnant."
The jockeys will hold their final training race in the UAE's emirate of Abu Dhabi on Monday, and Skeikh Zaid is expected to attend the event, Fuchtel said.
"We have some presents for him to say thank you, including some pictures of the camels he sent to the farm," he said.
Fuchtel said the desert-dwellers had adapted well to the cold weather in Germany and managed to cope with this winter's record-breaking temperatures.
"It gets really cold in places like Kazakhstan too, and the camels are used to it. After all, it gets very cold in the desert at night too," he said.
